name: Rendering and Lighting Pipelines
text:
# Rendering and Lighting Pipelines


## Overview
This family defines the differentiable rendering pipelines that convert a set of 3D Gaussian primitives (or their variants) into 2D images by projecting them onto the camera plane and [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) them [G]. It solves the problem of efficiently rasterizing soft, view-dependent primitives while supporting inverse rendering tasks such as lighting estimation and [physical parameter optimization](#4111-physical-parameter-optimization.md) [G]. What sets these methods apart from standard rasterization is the use of [alpha blending](#5750-alpha-blending.md) or weighted-sum compositing over sorted or spatially hashed primitives, often augmented with volume-based occlusion or explicit geometric intersection for sharp features [G].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the core mechanism of projecting 3D primitives into 2D screen space and accumulating color based on depth order or spatial locality [G].
1. **Projection:** Primitives are transformed from [world space](#2511-voxel-coordinate-systems-and-conversion.md) to camera space [G].
2. **Rasterization:** Primitives are assigned to screen tiles [G]. Visibility is determined by bounding boxes or projected extents [G].
3. **Compositing:** Color is accumulated using [front-to-back alpha blending](#1141-front-to-back-compositing-unpremultiplied.md) or order-independent techniques [G].
4. **Sorting:** Most methods require sorting primitives by depth within tiles to ensure correct front-to-back compositing, although some variants use [spatial hashing](#5002-spatial-hashing.md) or cell-level sorting to approximate this or enable order-independent transparency [G].

## Subtopics

### [Duplex-GS](1988-duplex-gs.md)
A dual-hierarchy framework for real-time order-independent [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md). It combines alpha-blending with reformulated Weighted-Sum Rendering (WSR) to eliminate popping and transparency artifacts. Unlike vanilla OIT, it reintroduces physical constraints via cell-level transmittance decay, allowing [early termination](#4675-early-termination.md). It differs from Sort-free GS by using cell-level sorting for physically grounded transmittance.

### [LinPrim Differentiable Rendering Pipeline](2195-linprim-differentiable-rendering-pipeline.md)
Replaces Gaussian ellipsoids with convex polyhedra (octahedra/tetrahedra) to enable efficient volumetric rendering with bounded geometry. It solves the problem of reconstructing sharp geometric features by allowing gradients to backpropagate through explicit [ray-triangle intersections](#11312-ray-triangle-intersection.md) (Möller-Trumbore), distinguishing it from methods relying on implicit density fields.

### [GsplatVolumeLighting](2203-gsplatvolumelighting.md)
Integrates volume occlusion directly into the per-splat lighting evaluation loop. It ray-marches through a 3D density texture to compute transmittance for shadows, combined with per-light attenuation. Unlike methods treating volume as a post-process, it shares the 3D density texture with the splat evaluation.

### [NeILF Rendering and Loss Calculation](2920-neilf-rendering-and-loss-calculation.md)
Decomposes Gaussian Splatting features into diffuse, specular, and ambient components using a Blinn-Phong model. It supports inverse rendering via loss functions on depth, normals, and color sparsity.

### [4DGS-Volume-Cloud Two-Stage Relighting](4101-4dgs-volume-cloud-two-stage-relighting.md)
A two-stage pipeline for physically parameterized volume clouds. Stage 1 trains physical parameters (geometry, extinction, albedo, scattering) under a single sun. [Stage 2](#2672-texel-allocation-via-rate-distortion.md) freezes these and trains a global environment network for arbitrary sun direction relighting and sky atmospheric scattering.

### Opacity to Alpha Conversion
A minor variant involving the extraction and conversion loop for alpha values from raw opacity parameters to ensure they are in the valid range for blending [G].

### Alpha Blending for Non-Pinhole Cameras
After obtaining 2D Gaussian function values via adapted projection for non-pinhole cameras, alpha blending is performed to generate the final image, identical to the original 3D-GS compositing step [S2].

## Background
3D Gaussian Splatting was introduced by Kerbl et al. in 2023 [G]. The rendering pipeline relies on efficient rasterization of 2D Gaussians projected from 3D [G]. Subsequent works have adapted this pipeline for differentiable rendering, volume lighting, and physical parameter estimation [G]. Implementation details for JSplat are provided in [S1, unofficial].

## Sources
[S1] JSplat, https://github.com/javagl/JSplat, fetched 2026-10-30 (unofficial)
[S2] On the Error Analysis of 3D Gaussian Splatting and an Optimal Projection Strategy, https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-72643-9_15, fetched 2026-10-29
